description: Every command is guarded by `command -v skillctl`, which catches an install that has not been reloaded yet — not a platform without a build. The plugin's bin/ holds a shim that is always present, so once installed the guard always passes and the shim is what decides: it execs the matching binary, or prints where to get one and exits 0. Exit 0 is deliberate, and it means a PreToolUse check on an unsupported platform allows rather than refuses. A security check that breaks the session is a security check people remove, so the honest claim is detection where a build exists, and a message where one does not.

hooks.command: if command -v skillctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then skillctl hook session-start; else echo 'skilltrust: no skillctl binary for this platform; see https://github.com/random1st/skilltrust'; fi
if command -v skillctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then skillctl hook pre-skill; fi
